answer.text: Coupon cash flows cannot be reinvested at the yields prevalent when the investment was made

explanation.text: The Logic: Source p.67 defines reinvestment risk as the possibility that coupon cash flows cannot be reinvested at the yields prevalent when the investment was made, because interest rates change over time. The Trap: The other options describe market direction, exchange-rate regimes, or tax changes, none of which is reinvestment risk per p.67. Note: The risk relates to reinvesting interim cash flows, not to the price movement of the original bond.
